rows.jp: 「それより、部活しませんか？」
rows.en: “Why don’t we do some club work instead?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "More importantly, shall we have activities?"
Misato: "...well."

rows.jp: 先輩がじっと見つめてくる。

ghs.en: Senpai gazes at me fixedly.

rows.jp: 「手伝いにきてくれたんですか？」

ghs.en: Misato: "Did you come to help me?"

rows.jp: 「はあ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sir!"
ghs.assessment: The source is a subdued acknowledgement or noncommittal response. The English changes it into a crisp form of address, altering the speech act and tone.
ghs.remedy: Use a subdued acknowledgement such as 'Yeah' or 'Uh-huh.'

rows.jp: 「そうですか」

ghs.en: Misato: "So you did."

rows.jp: 凝然と、固定された目線が外れない。
rows.en: Her gaze stayed fixed on me, unblinking.

ghs.en: Her stationary, congealed sight does not move from me.

rows.jp: やがて先輩の顔がふっとほころぶ。
rows.en: At last, Miyasumi’s face softened into a smile.

ghs.en: Eventually, Senpai's face puffs into the broadest of smiles.
ghs.assessment: Her face gently relaxes or opens into a smile. 'Puffs' gives the wrong physical motion, while 'the broadest' adds an unsupported superlative.
ghs.remedy: Describe her face softly relaxing into a smile without the superlative.

highlights.text: puffs into the broadest of smiles

rows.jp: 「ありがとうございます、ぺけくん」

ghs.en: Misato: "Thank you very much, Peke-kun."

rows.jp: 「いえ、帝国軍人として当然であります」
rows.en: “All in a day’s duty for a soldier of the Empire, ma’am.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "'Tis nothing, ma'am, it is the ordinary for a soldier of the Empire."
ghs.assessment: He mock-formally says that helping is only natural for an imperial soldier. The English uses the adjective 'ordinary' as a noun and produces an ungrammatical military-register line.
ghs.remedy: Use 'only natural for a soldier of the Empire' or an equivalent mock-formal expression.

highlights.text: it is the ordinary for a soldier of the Empire

rows.jp: 敬礼。

ghs.en: Salute!

rows.jp: 彼女はくすくすと笑う。

ghs.en: She laughs with a giggle.

rows.jp: 「でも残念ですが、今日はもう夜になってしまうのでした」

ghs.en: Misato: "It is too bad, but the day has already turned to night."
ghs.assessment: She says that the day is about to give way to night, explaining why the activity must end. The English states that night has already arrived, changing the temporal relation.
ghs.remedy: Say that it is already going to be night or is getting late.

highlights.text: the day has already turned to night

rows.jp: 「楽しい部活の時間は、おしまい」

ghs.en: Misato: "The time for fun club activity is all done."

rows.jp: 「えー」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Eeeh?"

rows.jp: 「すいませんね、一人でやるって決めていたので、時間は流動的だったりするんです」
rows.en: “Sorry. I’d planned on doing this alone, so my schedule is rather fluid.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Sorry, because I decided to do this on my own, the hours are fluid."

rows.jp: 「でも一人じゃ終わらないですよ？　配線だってあるでしょうし」
rows.en: “But you’ll never finish alone. You’ll need to run wiring, and—”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But alone you cannot finish this, right? There is the wiring."

rows.jp: 「そもそも電源だって」
rows.en: “You don’t even have a power source—”

ghs.en: Taichi: "For starters, there is the electricity."

rows.jp: 「平気ですよ」

ghs.en: Misato: "It is alright!"

rows.jp: 「女は度胸です」

ghs.en: Misato: "Women are pluck."
ghs.assessment: Pluck correctly means courage. The only confirmed defect is the malformed slogan-like predicate Women are pluck.

rows.jp: 「じゃ男は愛ですね」
rows.en: “Then a man’s got to have love.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Then men pluck them out."

rows.jp: 「先輩、ぼかぁ、ぼかぁ―――」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Senpai, pwease, pwease---"
ghs.assessment: ぼかぁ is a slurred or drawn-out contraction of 僕は, not securely a childish deformation. Pwease still replaces the failed self-reference with an unsupported plea.

rows.jp: にじり寄ろうとすると、
rows.en: As I began to edge closer—

ghs.en: I go to sidle up and,

rows.jp: 「部活しゅーりょーっ！」

ghs.en: Misato: "Cluuub haaas concludeeed!"

rows.jp: 「ぐぶぅっ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "G'buh!"

rows.jp: 顔面を片手で突き押され、よりさらに不細工になる俺。
rows.en: She planted one hand on my face and shoved, making me uglier still.

ghs.en: With one hand she squeezes on my face, turning me ever more ugly.
ghs.assessment: She pushes or shoves his face away with one hand. The English changes the forceful pushing action into squeezing his face.
ghs.remedy: Describe her pushing his face away with one hand.

rows.jp: 『ぐぶぅ』とか言っちゃってもうマリアナ海溝の底まで落ちたって感じ。
rows.en: That single “gubuh” sent me plummeting to the bottom of the Mariana Trench.

ghs.en: And blurting stuff like that "g'buh" felt like having fallen to the bottom of the Marianas Trench.

rows.jp: 「さ、帰りましょう。と言いましても、あなたとわたしは帰る方向も正反対ですけれど、ほほほほ」
rows.en: “Now, let’s go home. Of course, you and I are headed in opposite directions. Ho ho ho ho.”

ghs.en: Misato: "So! Let's go home. And I remind you, that my way home and yours are in the exact opposite direction, hohohohoh!"

rows.jp: 「……なーんか、釈然としません」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...whaaat, this cannot be fully satisfying!"

rows.jp: 「だって、今日はとても楽しかったでしょう？」
rows.en: “But you certainly had fun today, didn’t you?”

ghs.en: Misato: "But still, today was really fun, was it not?"

rows.jp: 「んー、どうでしょうねー」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hmmm, was it now..."

rows.jp: 「わたしの胸に顔をうずめてる時、お尻触ってましたよね？」
rows.en: “While you had your face buried in my chest, you were groping my butt, weren’t you?”

ghs.en: Misato: "When you were with your face buried in my chest, you were touching my butt, right?"
Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: 「ぐにぐにーって、すごい触り方で」

ghs.en: Misato: "With plenty of squeeze, and you going all 'squishity-squish!'"

rows.jp: 「しかも両手で」

ghs.en: Misato: "And furthermore, with both hands."
Taichi: "......"

rows.jp: 「くすぐったかったです」

ghs.en: Misato: "And it tickled."
Taichi: "～♪"

rows.jp: あさっての方角に向けて、口笛を吹く。
rows.en: I looked off toward next Tuesday and whistled.

ghs.en: So I whistled when faced with this derailing of thoughts.
ghs.assessment: He physically turns toward a completely unrelated direction and whistles, using the idiom 'toward the day after tomorrow.' The English removes the physical direction and replaces it with an abstract derailment of thought.
ghs.remedy: Describe him whistling while looking off in a random or unrelated direction.

highlights.text: when faced with this derailing of thoughts

rows.jp: 「オ・ト・コ・ノ・コ、なんですものねー」

ghs.en: Misato: "Be-ca-use-you-are-a-boooy, are you!"
ghs.assessment: She pointedly concludes that this is because he is a boy. The English appends an inverted interrogative tag to the already stated cause, producing the wrong syntax and rhetorical force.
ghs.remedy: Use an emphatic assertion such as 'Because you're a boy, after all.'

rows.jp: こめかみのあたりを、ぐりぐりとつつかれる。
rows.en: She dug a finger into my temple and ground it around.

ghs.en: She drills back and forth right on my temples.

rows.jp: けっこう痛い。

ghs.en: It's fairly painful.

rows.jp: ごまかせるはずもなかったのだ。
rows.en: There was no playing that off.

ghs.en: I could never swindle my way out of this.

rows.jp: 「うう……すいません……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ngggh... sorryyy..."

rows.jp: 「さて、どうしたものやら」
rows.en: “Now, what am I to do with you?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Well then, what am I to do with this."

rows.jp: 「わたしも、そのくらいの価値はある女だったってことですかね」
rows.en: “So I’m a woman worth at least that much to you?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Would that mean I, myself, am a woman with about that kind of value?"
ghs.assessment: She wonders whether the past incident means she was a woman worth that much to him. The English shifts the marked past-tense reflection into a present-tense statement about her general identity.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the retrospective 'was a woman worth that much' framing.

highlights.text: am a woman with about that kind of value

rows.jp: 「それともぺけくんが無節操なだけですかねー？」
rows.en: “Or will you monkey around with anything in a skirt, X?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Or is it that you are merely unprincipled, Peke-kun?"

rows.jp: 「いやいやいや、虚無僧ではありますが無節操などには！」
rows.en: “No, no, no! I may be a monk, but I’m no monkey!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "NoNnoNno, I may be a Komusou, but unprincipled, really!"
ghs.assessment: He protests that although he may be a komusou, he is not indiscriminate. The ellipsis-dependent Japanese denial is not completed in English, leaving an ungrammatical phrase that can read as an admission of the accusation.
ghs.remedy: Complete the denial: 'I may be a komusou, but I'm not indiscriminate.'

rows.jp: 「奴らと同列にされては困ります！！」
rows.en: “Don’t lump me in with those beasts!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Putting me side by side with that sort worries me!!!"

rows.jp: 必死に誤魔化す俺の、緊急ギャグは果てしなく寒い。
rows.en: My desperate emergency joke was cold enough to hit absolute zero.

ghs.en: When I'm desperate to deceive, my Emergency Jokes are endlessly lame.

rows.jp: 「ふふふ」

ghs.en: Misato: "Heh heh heh!"

rows.jp: 夕刻の、さらに濃度を増したオレンジを背景に、先輩は体をすこし傾けて、言った。
rows.en: Against the deepening orange of evening, Miyasumi leaned slightly to one side and said:

ghs.en: In this evening hour, in this scene where the density of orange grows ever more, Senpai leaned her body just a little and spoke.

rows.jp: 「許してあげますから、帰って反省タイムです」
rows.en: “I’ll forgive you. Now go home and think about what you’ve done.”

ghs.en: Misato: "I will forgive you for now, so it is time to go home and reflect."

rows.jp: 「さようなら、ですよ。ぺけくん」

ghs.en: Misato: "This is goodbye, then, Peke-kun."

rows.jp: 校舎を出て、屋上を見上げた。
rows.en: I left the school building and looked up at the roof.

ghs.en: I left the school building, and looked up at the rooftop.

rows.jp: アンテナが立っていた。

ghs.en: There the antenna stood.

rows.jp: その隣。

ghs.en: And next to it,

rows.jp: 先輩はまだ、そこにいる。

ghs.en: Senpai was, once more, still there,

rows.jp: 作業していた。

ghs.en: working, blue collar,
ghs.assessment: The source simply says that she was working. The English adds a blue-collar social or occupational characterization that is absent and does not fit the linked sentence.

rows.jp: もうじき夜になるのに。

ghs.en: even when it will soon be night,

rows.jp: 一人で。

ghs.en: alone.

rows.jp: この時になってはじめて。

ghs.en: And it was at this moment that, for the first time,

rows.jp: やんわりと、手伝いを拒絶されたのだと気づいた。
rows.en: that she had gently refused my help.

ghs.en: I realized that help had been refused, with gentleness.
